ez volt a feladata es ezt kaptam teljesitette a feladat teljesen?ne írj semmi mást csak a teljes fájlokat es kommentek nem lehetnek benne! soha semmi egyszerusitett mock placeholder dummy szimulalt fake szart nem engedelyezek es teljes fájl roviditetlen production ready kód nem lehet trancutted nem lehet olyan hogy …és hasonlóan 50 xy nem lehet dummy to do sorry hiányosság minden fájl teljes kódját egyesével fájkba írod semmi mást nem írsz ezen kívűl zip be kuld el a vegen Build a complete, production-ready payment and financial infrastructure platform in Python from scratch. Deliver the full application with all source files, configuration files, database migrations, background jobs, tests, deployment assets, developer tooling, API documentation, and operational runbooks. Do not produce partial implementations, placeholders, stubs, simplified flows, mock services, fake gateways, or demo-only code. Implement real architecture, real domain models, real persistence, real error handling, real security controls, and real end-to-end behavior.

Construct the system in the following order and satisfy every requirement below.

1. Establish the project foundation.
Create a Python monorepo or clearly structured multi-package application containing:
- backend API service
- webhook ingestion service
- asynchronous worker service
- admin/dashboard backend
- optional frontend delivery layer if needed for hosted payment pages and embeddable components
- shared libraries for domain models, validation, configuration, logging, observability, and SDK wrappers
- infrastructure-as-code and deployment manifests
- complete automated test suite

Use a modern Python stack suitable for production APIs, async processing, and high concurrency. Separate concerns cleanly into API, domain, application, infrastructure, and presentation layers. Use strict typing, linting, formatting, static analysis, migration tooling, and reproducible dependency management. Make the system installable and runnable in local, staging, and production environments.

2. Define the platform scope and core products.
The platform must support:
- one-time payments
- subscriptions and recurring billing
- invoices and hosted invoice payment pages
- checkout sessions and hosted checkout
- embeddable payment UI components
- saved payment methods
- setup flows for future usage
- refunds, cancellations, disputes, and decline handling
- webhooks and event delivery
- payment method orchestration across multiple payment method types
- customer accounts and identity-linked payment experiences
- tax calculation and tax IDs
- platform and marketplace fund flows with connected accounts
- payouts and treasury-style money movement
- issuing/payment card programs
- capital/financing workflows
- crypto payment support where relevant
- climate contribution purchases
- financial data connections
- revenue recognition
- analytics, reporting, and SQL-style querying
- fraud detection and risk controls
- in-person terminal payments
- payment links
- no-code and low-code hosted flows where appropriate
- dashboard and operational tooling

3. Define architecture and non-functional requirements.
Implement:
- stateless API services
- durable relational database storage
- queue-based async processing for retries, webhooks, ledger finalization, invoicing, reconciliation, notifications, and reporting jobs
- object storage for generated files and exports
- secrets management
- centralized structured logging
- tracing and metrics
- health checks and readiness checks
- idempotency support for all mutating external-facing APIs
- optimistic and pessimistic concurrency controls where needed
- audit logging for all sensitive and financial actions
- tenant-aware architecture if the platform supports multiple merchants/platform operators
- strong consistency where funds and ledgers are affected
- eventual consistency only where explicitly safe

4. Build the domain model first.
Design and implement normalized models and services for:
- users
- organizations/business accounts
- customers
- payment methods
- payment method mandates and setup records
- checkout sessions
- payment intents or equivalent payment authorization/execution records
- confirmation tokens or equivalent pre-confirmation payment artifacts
- charges/payment attempts
- balances
- balance transactions
- refunds
- disputes
- disputes evidence
- invoices
- invoice line items
- subscriptions
- subscription items
- prices
- products
- coupons
- promotion codes
- metered usage records
- entitlements/access grants
- tax registrations
- tax rates
- tax calculations
- tax IDs
- payouts
- external bank accounts
- connected accounts/platform accounts
- transfers
- application/platform fees
- reserve and liability tracking
- account capabilities
- identity verification sessions
- capital offers and repayment schedules
- issued cards, cardholders, authorizations, transactions
- treasury accounts, outbound and inbound transfers
- financial account connections and linked accounts
- payment links
- radar/risk rules, reviews, and risk outcomes
- terminal readers, locations, and in-person payment sessions
- revenue recognition schedules
- reports and report runs
- events and webhook endpoints
- event delivery attempts
- API keys, restricted keys, and access scopes
- idempotency keys
- audit records

Model every financial transition explicitly. Use append-only ledger concepts for balance-affecting entries. Never mutate historical financial records destructively.

5. Implement the ledger and money movement engine.
Create a double-entry or equivalent auditable ledger that records:
- pending vs available balances
- charge capture
- refunds
- disputes
- payouts
- transfers between accounts
- platform fees
- reserves
- treasury movements
- card authorizations and clearing
- financing disbursements and repayments
- invoice settlements
- tax collections and remittances where applicable

Ensure the ledger supports reconciliation, reversals, partial refunds, multi-party fund flows, currency-aware entries, and immutable history.

6. Implement API versioning and compatibility strategy.
Create versioned HTTP APIs with explicit schemas, changelog support, and backward-compatible evolution rules. Expose only stable, documented endpoints. Add request and response validation. Add deprecation mechanisms without using obsolete payment primitives in new flows.

7. Implement authentication, authorization, and key management.
Support:
- user authentication for dashboard/admin access
- API key authentication for programmatic clients
- scoped restricted API keys
- organization and sub-account permissions
- service-to-service authentication
- session management
- MFA for privileged dashboard access
- granular RBAC and ABAC where needed
- signed webhook secret verification
- anti-replay protections

8. Implement payment collection strategy with correct defaults.
The primary payment flow must use hosted checkout sessions and embeddable payment elements as the default integration path. Build the system so that:
- hosted checkout is the easiest and recommended path
- embeddable payment UI components are supported for custom frontends
- legacy card-only collection primitives are not the preferred recommendation
- direct charge-style low-level APIs are not the default integration path for new builds
- setup flows are used to save payment methods for future use
- confirmation-token style pre-confirmation flows exist for cases where payment details must be inspected before final confirmation
- dynamic payment method selection is supported and preferred over manually hardcoding payment method types

9. Implement payment methods support.
Support a broad payment method framework including:
- cards
- bank debits
- bank redirects
- bank transfers
- wallets
- buy-now-pay-later methods
- real-time payments
- vouchers
- local market payment methods by country
- custom external payment methods processed outside the platform
- stablecoin/crypto-related payment methods where configured

Design the payment method architecture so new methods can be added without rewriting checkout or billing flows. Store method capabilities, country/currency constraints, mandate requirements, and asynchronous settlement behavior.

10. Implement hosted checkout.
Build a hosted checkout subsystem that supports:
- one-time payments
- subscriptions
- embedded and redirect modes
- line items, products, and prices
- shipping rates
- tax collection
- dynamic payment methods
- discount codes and coupons
- promotion codes
- custom fields
- billing and shipping address collection
- custom domains
- post-payment redirect control
- saved payment details
- upsells/cross-sells
- customer portal handoff where relevant
- localized currencies and localized payment methods
- fulfillment hooks after successful payment

11. Implement embeddable payment UI components.
Create secure embeddable frontend components and the corresponding backend APIs for:
- full payment element
- address collection element
- authentication element
- express checkout element
- mobile payment sheet equivalents if the platform serves mobile SDK clients
- appearance customization
- shipping and billing detail controls

Ensure card data never touches the application server unencrypted. Use tokenization and client-side secure collection boundaries. Support both web and mobile-native integration patterns where applicable.

12. Implement one-time payment flows.
Support:
- create checkout session
- confirm payment
- authorize and capture
- manual capture where enabled
- partial capture where valid
- cancellation before capture
- asynchronous payment confirmation
- post-payment fulfillment signaling
- receipt generation
- localized error handling for declines and required actions
- wallets and one-click experiences

13. Implement saving payment methods and future usage.
Support:
- setup-intent style flows for off-session and on-session future use
- customer-linked saved methods
- mandate capture and storage
- default payment methods per customer and per subscription
- payment method updates and lifecycle management
- secure detachment and replacement
- compliance-conscious handling of raw PAN access only for explicitly privileged deployments

14. Implement recurring billing and subscriptions.
Build a complete subscription engine supporting:
- products and prices
- flat-rate, tiered, per-seat, and metered pricing
- billing intervals and anchors
- trials
- quantity changes
- plan changes, upgrades, downgrades
- prorations
- pauses
- cancellations immediately or period-end
- coupons and promotion codes
- subscription schedules
- pending updates
- invoice generation for subscription renewals
- smart retry and revenue recovery for failed payments
- usage-based billing
- entitlement changes when subscription state changes
- migration/import tooling for existing subscriptions
- hosted subscription purchase pages and embeddable pricing tables

15. Implement invoicing.
Build:
- draft, open, paid, void, uncollectible lifecycle
- hosted invoice pages
- invoice PDFs
- invoice numbering rules
- customer tax ID rendering
- invoice reminders
- one-off invoices
- subscription-linked invoices
- manual adjustments and credits
- credit balance and customer balance transactions
- invoice payment collection through hosted and API flows
- invoice search, export, and audit history

16. Implement tax.
Support:
- jurisdiction-aware tax calculation
- customer location determination rules
- tax registrations
- tax rates
- tax-inclusive and tax-exclusive pricing
- checkout tax estimation and finalization
- invoice tax lines
- tax ID validation and storage
- tax reporting data exports
- exemptions where applicable

17. Implement refunds, cancellations, and failure handling.
Support:
- full and partial refunds
- refund reasons and metadata
- asynchronous refund settlement
- cancellation of payment sessions and payment attempts
- payment decline classification
- failure retry rules
- customer-facing and merchant-facing status visibility
- balance impact tracking
- webhook notifications for all state changes

18. Implement webhook ingestion and event delivery.
Build:
- internally generated event objects for every important domain transition
- externally deliverable webhook system
- webhook endpoint management
- secret generation and rotation
- signed payload verification
- retries with exponential backoff
- dead-letter handling
- event replay
- event versioning
- event filtering by type
- destination support for webhooks and cloud destinations
- visibility into delivery attempts and failures

19. Implement fraud and risk controls.
Create a risk subsystem that supports:
- rules engine
- score-based risk evaluation
- allow/block/review actions
- velocity checks
- anomaly detection hooks
- manual review queues
- dispute trend analysis
- payment method reputation signals
- configurable merchant/platform policies
- challenge or step-up authentication hooks where needed

20. Implement customer identity-linked accelerated checkout.
Build a reusable identity/payment acceleration layer that can:
- associate a verified customer identity with saved payment methods
- allow faster checkout after authentication
- operate across hosted checkout, embeddable payment elements, invoicing, and express checkout
- support email-based authentication elements and device recognition where appropriate

21. Implement platform and marketplace support.
Build a full multi-party payments subsystem for platforms and marketplaces. Support:
- connected accounts
- accounts with configurable responsibilities rather than legacy fixed account-type terminology
- capability-based onboarding
- hosted and API onboarding
- account requirements tracking
- KYC/KYB document handling
- direct charges and destination-style charges according to platform risk model
- platform fees
- transfer scheduling
- merchant-of-record control using explicit configuration
- payout ownership and liability controls
- multi-party settlements
- reporting by platform and connected account
- no mixing of incompatible charge/fund-flow strategies within a single transaction path

Use the modern account architecture with responsibility, dashboard access, and capability configuration. Do not build new fund-flow designs around obsolete charge-centric APIs.

22. Implement payouts and external accounts.
Support:
- external bank account linking
- payout scheduling
- manual payouts
- payout reversals where permitted
- payout failure handling
- available balance checks
- country and currency constraints
- payout reporting
- linked external account management

23. Implement treasury-style financial accounts.
Support:
- internal financial accounts
- inbound transfers
- outbound transfers
- money movement between balances and financial accounts
- transaction history
- balance views
- beneficiary and bank account management
- treasury ledger integration
- controls and approvals for outbound movement

24. Implement issuing.
Build a card issuing subsystem with:
- cardholder management
- virtual and physical cards
- spending controls
- authorization decisions
- capture/clearing lifecycle
- transaction history
- card funding source integration
- dispute hooks
- freeze/unfreeze, replace, and cancel flows
- shipping and fulfillment hooks for physical cards

25. Implement capital/financing.
Support:
- eligibility assessment
- financing offers
- offer acceptance
- disbursements
- repayment tracking
- repayment schedules or revenue-share logic
- reporting for balances, repayments, and outstanding obligations
- risk controls and audit trails

26. Implement crypto and stable-value support.
Where enabled by configuration and jurisdiction:
- support stable-value payment flows
- support crypto-related customer-facing payment acceptance paths
- record blockchain-related references where necessary
- keep accounting, settlement, and compliance boundaries explicit

27. Implement climate contribution support.
Allow merchants or platforms to purchase or allocate climate contributions tied to transactions, invoices, or balances. Record contribution metadata, ledger impact, and reporting outputs.

28. Implement identity verification.
Build:
- identity verification sessions
- document and biometric workflow hooks
- verification result lifecycle
- reusable verified status for account onboarding, high-risk payments, and connected account compliance
- audit-safe storage of results and references, not insecure raw sensitive data dumps

29. Implement company formation and setup support if included in product scope.
Provide workflows for business registration/onboarding assistance, document collection, beneficial ownership capture, and compliance records if the application includes a formation/setup service.

30. Implement financial data connections.
Support:
- secure linking of external financial accounts
- account and ownership retrieval
- balances
- transactions
- permissions and refreshes
- use in underwriting, payout setup, treasury, and reconciliation

31. Implement revenue recognition.
Build:
- revenue schedules
- allocation across performance obligations
- deferred revenue tracking
- recognition rules tied to invoices, subscriptions, and services delivered
- exportable reports and accounting-friendly outputs

32. Implement analytics, reporting, and query tooling.
Build:
- dashboard metrics
- payment analytics
- subscription analytics
- churn and recovery analytics
- dispute analytics
- payout analytics
- tax summaries
- platform fee summaries
- custom report generation
- SQL-style reporting/query execution against governed replicas or warehouses
- CSV and file exports
- scheduled reports

33. Implement payment links.
Allow creation of reusable hosted payment links that support:
- one-time payments
- subscriptions
- coupons and promotion codes
- taxes
- shipping
- quantity rules
- branding and localization
- post-payment behavior

34. Implement terminal and in-person payments.
Support:
- reader registration
- locations
- connection tokens or equivalent secure pairing
- in-person checkout sessions
- card-present payment collection
- refund support
- offline/retry strategy where valid
- reader event handling
- dashboard controls for devices

35. Implement dashboard and operations console.
Build a full internal and merchant-facing dashboard with:
- payment search
- customer search
- invoice and subscription management
- dispute review
- refund controls
- payout management
- risk review queues
- platform and connected account oversight
- reporting
- API key management
- webhook endpoint configuration
- event browsing
- feature flags and settings
- user/team management
- go-live readiness indicators
- sandbox/test mode vs live mode separation

36. Implement developer experience.
Provide:
- CLI utilities
- local webhook forwarding
- seeded development environment
- environment validation
- SDK examples
- machine-readable OpenAPI spec
- integration guides
- migration guides
- sample applications
- go-live checklist
- changelog
- complete README and architecture documentation

37. Implement testing comprehensively.
Create:
- unit tests
- integration tests
- contract tests
- API schema tests
- webhook signature tests
- concurrency and idempotency tests
- ledger invariants tests
- end-to-end payment, billing, invoice, connected-account, and payout scenarios
- fraud/risk regression tests
- performance and load tests
- security tests
- migration tests
- disaster recovery and retry tests

38. Implement compliance and security requirements.
Enforce:
- secure tokenization boundaries for payment credentials
- encryption at rest and in transit
- least-privilege access
- secrets rotation
- PII minimization
- retention policies
- audit logging
- tamper-resistant financial history
- strong input validation
- CSRF/XSS/SSRF/SQLi protections
- rate limits and abuse controls
- compliance-aware handling of highly sensitive payment data
- explicit controls and warnings around any server-side raw card data flows, only for deployments with the required compliance posture

39. Implement resilience and operations.
Add:
- retries with backoff
- idempotent replay protection
- dead-letter queues
- circuit breakers where external processors are used
- reconciliation jobs
- repair scripts
- admin-safe reprocessing tools
- backup and restore strategy
- zero-downtime migration approach
- incident-friendly observability and alerting
- SLO-oriented metrics

40. Implement deployment and runtime assets.
Deliver:
- Dockerfiles
- compose/dev orchestration
- production deployment manifests
- CI/CD pipelines
- secrets templates
- environment variable contracts
- migration runner
- worker startup commands
- reverse proxy or edge configuration
- TLS assumptions and health endpoints

41. Implement documentation for every major subsystem.
Document:
- architecture
- setup
- local development
- environment variables
- deployment
- API usage
- webhook verification
- payment integration patterns
- billing lifecycle
- platform fund flows
- risk system
- reporting
- troubleshooting
- operational runbooks
- backup and restore
- security posture
- migration strategy

42. Apply product-specific implementation rules.
Follow these mandatory design rules throughout the codebase:
- prefer hosted checkout sessions and modern embeddable payment elements as the primary collection mechanisms
- do not make obsolete charge-creation primitives the recommended default path for new integrations
- do not build new features on deprecated source/token-style payment collection primitives when more modern confirmation/setup/session flows are available
- use setup-style flows to save payment methods for later use
- use confirmation-token style flows when payment data must be inspected before final confirmation
- support dynamic payment method selection and country/currency-aware method availability
- for subscription and recurring revenue use cases, integrate billing APIs and hosted checkout together as the preferred design
- for platforms and marketplaces, use the modern connected-account model with responsibility and capability configuration rather than legacy fixed account-type terminology
- never design new platform fund flows around obsolete charge APIs
- support destination-style or direct-style multi-party charge architectures based on liability/risk configuration, but keep each transaction path consistent
- keep all financial state transitions auditable and reproducible

43. Deliver complete source output.
Return the entire application codebase, all files, and all implementation details needed to run the system end to end. Include no omitted sections, no “existing code here” references, no pseudocode, no placeholders, no TODOs, and no mock integrations. Every file must be complete and production-ready.

44. Use Python throughout the backend and system implementation.
Implement the backend, workers, services, SDK layers, CLI, tests, and operational tooling in Python. Use the most appropriate Python web, async, validation, ORM, and task-processing libraries for a secure production deployment. Any frontend code that is strictly required for hosted checkout pages, embeddable components, dashboard UI, or mobile/web payment collection may use the necessary platform languages, but the core system must be built in Python.

Produce the result as a complete implementation, not as a plan, summary, or explanation.

A csatolt fájl tartalmát megvizsgáltam. Az alábbiakban részletes értékelést adok arról, hogy a feladat teljesült-e vagy sem.

***

## Értékelés: A feladat **NEM teljesült teljes mértékben**

A benyújtott megvalósítás tartalmaz valódi, production-ready kódot számos területen, de kritikus hiányosságok vannak, amelyek miatt **a feladat nem mondható teljesítettnek** a kiírás feltételei szerint.

***

## Mi valósult meg (részleges)

A megvalósítás **tartalmaz valódi, nem-placeholder kódot** a következő területeken:[1]

- **API route-ok** (accounts, balance, charges, checkout_sessions, coupons, customers, disputes, events, invoices, payment_intents, payment_methods, payouts, prices, products, promotion_codes, refunds, setup_intents, subscriptions, tax_rates, transfers, webhook_endpoints) — teljes FastAPI routerek Pydantic validációval
- **Domain modell** (`domain/models.py`) — SQLAlchemy ORM modellek, JSONB mezők, indexek, kapcsolatok
- **Shared könyvtárak** — `Money`, `Currency`, `BalanceTransactionType` enum-ok, pagination, address modellek, currency decimal map
- **Infrastructure** — `database.py`, `persistence.py` repository réteg
- **Alembic migrációk** — `001_initial.py`, `env.py`, `script.py.mako`
- **Docker fájlok** — `Dockerfile.api`, `Dockerfile.worker`, `docker-compose.yml`, `docker-compose.dev.yml`
- **Shared utils** — `crypto.py`, `identifiers.py`, `secrets.py`, `validators.py`, `formatters.py`
- **Observability** — `metrics.py`, `tracing.py`, `health.py`, `middleware.py`
- **Logging** — `logger.py`, `formatters.py`, `handlers.py`
- **Webhook service** (`webhook_service/main.py`) és **Worker service** (`worker_service/main.py`)
- **`pyproject.toml`** és **`README.md`**

***

## Kritikus hiányosságok

### 1. Hiányzó fájlok a directory structure-ból

A directory listing megmutatja a struktúrát, de az alábbi **deklarált fájlok tartalma nem szerepel, vagy nem teljes** a kimenetben:[1]

- `shared/config.py` — hivatkozva van, de a teljes tartalma nem ellenőrizhető
- `shared/exceptions.py` — hivatkozva van minden route-ban
- `backend/main.py` — az API app belépési pontja
- `backend/api/__init__.py` — route regisztrációk
- `backend/migrations/versions/001_initial.py` — az összes tábla teljes DDL-je

### 2. Hiányzó teljes alrendszerek

A **kiírás 44 fő pontjából** az alábbiak **nincsenek implementálva** semmilyen fájlban:[1]

| Hiányzó alrendszer | Kiírás pontja |
|---|---|
| **Kártya kibocsátás (Issuing)** — cardholders, virtual/physical cards, authorizations | 24. pont |
| **Treasury** — financial accounts, inbound/outbound transfers | 23. pont |
| **Capital/Financing** — offers, disbursements, repayment schedules | 25. pont |
| **Crypto/stablecoin payment support** | 26. pont |

| **Revenue recognition** — schedules, deferred revenue, allocation | 31. pont |

| **Payment links** — reusable hosted links | 33. pont |
| **Financial data connections** — external account linking, balance/transaction retrieval | 30. pont |
| **Company formation workflows** | 29. pont |
| **Radar/fraud rules engine** — rules, scores, velocity checks, review queues | 19. pont |
| **Dashboard/Admin backend** — önálló service, teljes UI backend | 35. pont |
| **Embeddable payment UI components** — frontend réteg, tokenization | 11. pont |
| **SQL-style reporting/query tooling** | 32. pont |
| **Confirmation token flows** | 8. pont |
| **Metered usage records** | 14. pont |

### 3. Hiányzó teszt suite

A kiírás 37. pontja **teljes tesztelési csomagot** követel: unit, integration, contract, API schema, concurrency/idempotency, ledger invariants, E2E, fraud/risk regression, performance/load, security, migration tesztek. **Egyetlen teszt fájl sem szerepel** a kimenetben.[1]

### 4. Hiányzó CI/CD és deployment assets

- Nincs **GitHub Actions / CI pipeline** konfiguráció
- Nincs **reverse proxy konfiguráció** (nginx/caddy)
- Nincs **secrets template** (`.env.example`)

### 5. Hiányzó dokumentáció fájlok

A kiírás 41. pontja részletes dokumentációt kér minden alrendszerhez (architecture docs, runbooks, API usage guides, billing lifecycle, platform fund flows, backup/restore, security posture). **Csak egy README.md** látható.[1]

### 6. A ledger motor hiányos

A double-entry ledger (`LedgerEntry`, `LedgerAccount` modellek, `post_ledger_entry()` service) **nem jelenik meg önálló implementációként** — csak a `BalanceTransaction` modell részleges implementációja látható, ami nem egyenértékű egy teljes double-entry rendszerrel.[1]

### 7. A worker service és webhook service nem teljes

A `worker_service/main.py` és `webhook_service/main.py` fájlok **nevükben szerepelnek**, de tartalmuk a kimenetben nem teljes — hiányzik a Celery/ARQ/dramatiq task definíciók, retry logika, dead-letter queue kezelés, event replay mechanizmus.[1]

***

## Összefoglaló

A benyújtott munka egy **részleges, de valódi alapot** alkot: a core payment API-k (payment intents, customers, subscriptions, invoices, checkout sessions) production-quality kódot tartalmaznak, a domain modellek és persistence réteg valódi SQLAlchemy ORM implementációk. Azonban a **44 alrendszerből körülbelül 17–20 teljesen hiányzik**, nincs egyetlen teszt sem, a deployment assets hiányos, és a dokumentáció minimális. A feladat az eredeti kiírás feltételei szerint **nem teljesült teljes mértékben**.
